# Genesis Apocryphon Column 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 5 | **Condition:** Fragmentary

---

**5:1** [...] Then Enoch spoke and said to his son Methuselah [...]

**5:2** [...] Go back and tell your son Lamech [...]

**5:3** [...] the child truly belongs to him, born from his own seed [...]

**5:4** [...] not from the Watchers [...] not from the sons of heaven [...]

**5:5** [...] this child [...] is indeed his own [...]

**5:6** [...] he shall be named Noah [...]

**5:7** [...] he will be a righteous man among you [...]

**5:8** [...] bringing rest and relief [...] to him and to his descendants [...]

**5:9** [...] through all the ages to come [...]

**5:10** [...] for a great devastation is coming upon the earth [...]

**5:11** [...] a great flood [...] bringing destruction for an entire year [...]

**5:12** [...] only he will survive [...] along with his sons [...]

**5:13** [...] the whole earth will become corrupt [...]

**5:14** [...] overrun with wickedness [...] and filled with violence [...]

**5:15** [...] but he will stand as [...] the righteous one [...] the man of integrity [...]

**5:16** [...]

**5:17** [...]

**5:18** [...]

**5:19** [...]

**5:20** [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 5 is the climactic resolution of the paternity narrative. Enoch, from his place at the edge of creation, confirms what Bitenosh swore: Noah is Lamech's son. But the reassurance carries a terrible prophecy — a flood that will destroy all life. Noah, whose very name means "rest," will be the sole survivor, the righteous anchor of a new humanity.*
